title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Sierra Leone, ICSP advanced health‑system strengthening by improving service quality across 80 assessed Peripheral Health Units, where 59 facilities (74%) met the required quality benchmark following clinical mentoring, joint supportive supervision and stronger district‑level oversight. These gains were reinforced by improved WASH and IPC conditions, supported through complementary investments in infrastructure and facility‑level WASH‑FIT planning. At the systems level, the Kingtom Faecal Sludge Treatment Plant achieved major operational improvements, processing 18,229 m³ of waste and implementing critical upgrades that enhanced public‑health protection for Freetown. Together, these efforts reduced vulnerability to health‑related shocks and strengthened district and national preparedness capacities.. Building resilience to shocks that impact health, such as disease outbreaks through a focus on Early Warning and Response Systems (EWRS) by working in collaboration with the NDMA.
